description:
Silent wrong answer -- the highest-severity correctness finding in the fz-5xp research.

  fz:      dbg("a#{1}b")   =>  "a#{1}b"
  Elixir:  IO.inspect("a#{1}b") =>  "a1b"

src/parser/lexer.rs:340 read_quoted_binary_bytes copies bytes verbatim; there is no
#{ handling anywhere. Recognised escapes are only \n \t \r \\ \" -- no \x, no
\uXXXX, no heredocs.

Until interpolation is implemented, an unescaped #{ inside a string literal must be a
lex error. Shipping a String module while interpolation silently no-ops would make
every error message in the library wrong.

Elixir's lowering is fully specified and mechanical (elixir_parser.yrl:1088) --
"a#{x}b" becomes <<"a", Kernel.to_string(x)::binary, "b">>, and fz already has
<<>> construction and <> concat. Implementing it needs String.Chars first.
title: String interpolation renders literally with no diagnostic
